target: AGRV2K LQFP-64 bench, first session on this physical unit
transport: CMSIS-DAP v2 over SWD, vendor-free agamemnon/openocd/agrv2k.cfg (agamemnon probe) and AGM tools/agm_supra openocd (raw mdw)
scope: DEVICE_ID/misa/DPIDR match the documented AG32VF303/AGRV2K RV32IMAFC silicon signature on a new LQFP-64 physical unit; this is a DAP/core-level check only and does not itself observe package pad bonding

action: read-only full 256KiB flash dump via DAP (dump_image 0x80000000 0x40000), taken before any other operation on this unit
scope: read-only pre-any-write factory backup with a byte-identical repeat-read determinism check; boot ROM is byte-identical to the previously backed-up L48 unit's boot ROM (tools/dumps/bootrom_00010000_8k.bin), consistent with a shared masked-ROM die across packages; does NOT qualify SPI flash contents as identical across units (flash is per-unit user data, not compared here beyond this unit's own two reads). No flash write of any kind occurred this session.

flow: agamemnon build --uarch (open toolchain; WSL oss-cad-suite yosys + pinned nextpnr-agrv2k build, no vendor binary)
device_env_result: rejected by claim_policy: release-strict emission is qualified only for AGRV2KL48; Q32, L64, and L100 remain recovered, unqualified post-release package data -- build proceeded under the default AGRV2KL48 legality model, which is honestly noted as a build-time-only distinction because the design instantiates zero physical pads
scope: first FCB config-accept of an AGaMEMnon open-toolchain (--uarch) bitstream on LQFP-64-packaged AGRV2K silicon, confirmed with two independent SRAM-injected firmware stubs; the design is pad-free so this demonstrates the die/FCB accepting the open bitgen's config stream, not any package-specific IO behavior

write_probe: 0xdeadbeef written to BANK+0x0; read back unchanged at 0x795fe3dd (write accepted, no effect)
cycle_sim_source: agamemnon build examples/designs/mcu_ahb_constant_slave.v --uarch --verify (routed-netlist sim of this exact routed_json_sha256)
finding: the endpoint behaves as a fully well-formed combinational External-AHB slave on L64 silicon (ready every cycle, one stable constant across 64 reads and 3 addresses, writes accepted without effect) -- but the observed constant does not match either this same build's own --verify cycle-simulation of the identical routed netlist (which predicts 0x4147414d) or the previously published L48 qualification value (also 0x4147414d). Both discrepant values come from THIS session's own build, so this is a sim-vs-bitstream (or bitgen LUT-encoding) discrepancy in the current open-toolchain state for this specific fresh nextpnr placement -- not attributed to the L64 package (zero physical pads are used) or to a silicon difference. Flagged for separate toolchain follow-up; not claimed as a reproduction of the L48-qualified 0x4147414d result.
scope: proves a real, protocol-correct AHB read+write transaction on L64 silicon over the open flow; does not reproduce the specific previously-qualified constant value on this fresh build

method: two-window MTIME (0x0200bff8/0x0200bffc) vs OpenOCD host wall-clock, same regression formula as tools/oracle_pll_60_8_mtime (a = (d2-d1)/(t2-t1))
measured_clock: boot-default (flash-resident boot ROM) SYSCLK, no custom clock switch applied for this measurement
pll_manual_switch_finding: the recovered SYS_SwitchPLLClock(0) RCC sequence (examples/firmware/clkcfg_stub.bin and tools/oracle_pll_60_8_mtime's stub) was exercised by direct register read/write over the DAP: RCC 0x0300000C bit4 (HSE ready) set promptly after enabling HSE+PLL, but bit6 (PLL lock) was not observed after ~3.3s of polling on this unit. Undiagnosed this session; flagged for follow-up and NOT claimed as an L64-package-specific limitation (the RCC block is MCU-side and package-agnostic).
scope: the MTIME two-window method itself works cleanly on L64 silicon and yields a real ~239.6MHz boot-default SYSCLK data point, consistent with the documented ~248MHz nominal core clock; the specific previously-qualified (60,8)=60MHz commanded PLL point was not reproduced this session

pcf_target_pin: PIN_22 (tile 19,13,0 -- the SAME tile as L48's silicon-qualified toggle-output PIN_16)
release_strict_attempt: agamemnon build --uarch --pcf with AGAMEMNON_DEVICE=AGRV2KL64: rejected by claim_policy (option:AGAMEMNON_DEVICE=AGRV2KL64: strict emission is qualified only for AGRV2KL48) -- confirmed this gate is a blanket package check independent of which physical tiles the PCF uses
research_unsafe_uarch_attempt: agamemnon build --uarch --pcf --research-unsafe: did not route (direct-D BEL packing conflict after cap/fanout escalation) -- not pursued further this session
working_flow: agamemnon build examples/designs/tff.v --pcf examples/constraints/tff_L64.pcf --research-unsafe (Python-architecture, non-uarch path) -- routed cleanly, 17/17 pips mapped, 0 unmapped
scope: desk-prep artifact for a later Pico-harness session (no board pad observation this session): confirms this pad-targeting bitstream FCB-config-accepts on real L64 silicon; does NOT qualify the pad electrically (no toggle/logic-level observation was made -- the Pico rig was not connected). Also documents that the release-strict --uarch --pcf path is hardcoded to AGRV2KL48 regardless of PCF tile choice, and that --uarch --research-unsafe does not currently route this design/PCF combination on L64 (unresolved, filed for follow-up); the non-uarch --research-unsafe path is the one that produced a usable image tonight.
